observation_summary: The MultiDirectional optimizer enters an infinite loop when the starting point is already the optimal solution, eventually exceeding the maximum iteration count.
hypothesis: The iterateSimplex method lacks a convergence check at the beginning of the iteration loop. When the initial simplex is already optimal, the algorithm continues to perform iterations (reflection, expansion, contraction) instead of terminating, leading to an infinite loop.
prediction: The fix will involve adding a convergence check within the iterateSimplex loop to detect if the current simplex has already converged to the optimum, allowing the method to return early.
experiment_rationale: The provided diff shows the addition of a convergence check (using a RealConvergenceChecker) inside the iterateSimplex method, which confirms that the algorithm was missing the logic to terminate when convergence was reached.
reasoning_summary: The bug is an infinite loop caused by missing convergence logic within the iterative procedure. The fix adds the necessary check to the loop, which is a procedural correction to the algorithm's termination strategy. It is not a simple guard (Checking) because it involves integrating a convergence check into the core optimization loop, and it is not a design-level capability issue (Function/Class/Object).
evidence_used: The bug report states: 'MultiDirectional.iterateSimplex loops forever if the starting point is the correct solution.'
The fix diff shows the addition of a convergence check (checker.converged) inside the iterateSimplex loop.
The stack trace shows the failure occurs due to 'Maximal number of iterations (100) exceeded'.

alternative_types.why_not_primary: While a check is added, the root cause is the absence of the convergence termination logic within the algorithm's loop, which is a procedural/algorithmic flaw rather than a simple parameter validation guard.
